title: Spec of a ring map is formally smooth iff the ring map has the square-zero lifting property
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ the induced morphism of affine schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ is formally smooth in the sense of [def-sbc-formally-smooth] (lifting along first order thickenings $T\subset T'$ of affine schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]) if and only if $\varphi$ is a formally smooth ring map in the sense of Stacks Algebra, Definition 00TI: for every commutative ring $D$ with a ring map $R\to D$, every ideal $N\subseteq D$ with $N^2=0$, with quotient map $q:D\to D/N$, and every homomorphism of $R$-algebras $g:S\to D/N$, there is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $f:S\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 02H4 (lemma-affine-formally-smooth, line 3164; 'immediate from the definitions' 02H0 and Algebra 00TI 'by the equivalence of categories of rings and affine schemes', Schemes, Lemma Tag 01I2, schemes-lemma-category-affine-schemes); Algebra, Definition Tag 00TI (definition-formally-smooth, algebra.tex line 37805)

proof.text: *Notation and the dictionary of morphisms.* Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $f=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:X\to Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\operatorname{Spec}$ is contravariant and functorial ($\operatorname{Spec}(\psi\circ\chi)=\operatorname{Spec}\chi\circ\operatorname{Spec}\psi$), every morphism of schemes $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\chi$ for exactly one ring map $\chi:A\to B$, and $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}(\operatorname{Spec}A)=A$, the ring map induced by $\operatorname{Spec}\chi$ on global sections being $\chi$. Consequently, for a ring $D$ with structure map $\beta:R\to D$ (so $\operatorname{Spec}D$ is a scheme over $Y$ via $\operatorname{Spec}\beta$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]) and a ring map $h:S\to D$: $\operatorname{Spec}h$ is a morphism over $Y$, i.e. $f\circ\operatorname{Spec}h=\operatorname{Spec}\beta$, iff $\operatorname{Spec}(h\circ\varphi)=\operatorname{Spec}\beta$, iff $h\circ\varphi=\beta$, i.e. iff $h$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras.

*Square-zero quotients give first order thickenings of affine schemes.* Let $D$ be a ring with $\beta:R\to D$, $N\subseteq D$ an ideal with $N^2=0$, $q:D\to D/N$ the quotient map, $T'=\operatorname{Spec}D$ over $Y$ via $\operatorname{Spec}\beta$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}(D/N)$ and $i=\operatorname{Spec}q:T\to T'$. By the first step the map induced by $i$ on global sections $\mathcal O_{T'}(T')=D\to\mathcal O_T(i^{-1}T')=\mathcal O_T(T)=D/N$ is $q$, which is surjective, and $i^{-1}(T')=T$ is affine; applying [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](2) to the covering of $T'$ by the single affine open $T'$, $i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] satisfies, on the affine open $U=T'$ where $i$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(D/N)\to\operatorname{Spec}D$, $\mathcal I(T')=\ker q=N$ and $\mathcal I=\widetilde N$. By the definition of products of quasi-coherent ideals [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], on the affine open $T'$ itself $\mathcal I^2=(\mathcal I(T')\mathcal I(T'))^\sim=(N^2)^\sim=0$. Hence $T\subset T'$ is a first order thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] of affine schemes over $Y$, $T$ being over $Y$ through $\operatorname{Spec}\beta\circ i=\operatorname{Spec}(q\circ\beta)$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion, line 58), (1)=>(2) and (3)=>(1); Schemes, Lemma Tag 01IH (lemma-closed-immersion-affine-case, schemes.tex line 1600)

proof.text: *Every first order thickening of affine schemes is of this form.* Let $T\subset T'$ be a first order thickening of affine schemes over $Y$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], with closed immersion $i:T\to T'$, structure morphism $b:T'\to Y$ and ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$, $\mathcal I^2=0$. Since $T'$ is affine [def-pc-scheme], choose an isomorphism $T'\cong\operatorname{Spec}D$; then $D\cong\mathcal O_{T'}(T')$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](1) applied to the affine open $V=T'$, the ring map $i^\sharp:D=\mathcal O_{T'}(T')\to C=\mathcal O_T(T)$ is surjective; let $N=\ker i^\sharp$, so $i^\sharp$ induces an isomorphism $D/N\cong C$, and $T$ is affine, $T\cong\operatorname{Spec}C\cong\operatorname{Spec}(D/N)$. Under these isomorphisms $i$ becomes a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(D/N)\to\operatorname{Spec}D$, which by the first step is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the ring map it induces on global sections, namely $q:D\to D/N$. By [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] $\mathcal I(T')=\ker(\mathcal O_{T'}(T')\to\mathcal O_T(T))=N$, and by [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers] (square zero means $\mathcal I(U)^2=0$ on every affine open $U$; take $U=T'$) $N^2=0$. Finally $b=\operatorname{Spec}\beta$ for a unique $\beta:R\to D$ (first step), making $D$ an $R$-algebra. So the thickening $(T\subset T',b)$ is isomorphic, by isomorphisms compatible with $i$ and with the morphisms to $Y$, to the thickening $(\operatorname{Spec}(D/N)\subset\operatorname{Spec}D,\operatorname{Spec}\beta)$ of the second step with $N^2=0$.

proof.text: *Transport along isomorphisms.* If two first order thickenings over $Y$, $(T_1\subset T_1',b_1)$ and $(T_2\subset T_2',b_2)$, are related by isomorphisms $\sigma:T_1\to T_2$, $\sigma':T_1'\to T_2'$ with $i_2\sigma=\sigma'i_1$ and $b_2\sigma'=b_1$, then $a\mapsto a\sigma^{-1}$, $a'\mapsto a'\sigma'^{-1}$ is a bijection between the lifting problems of [def-sbc-formally-smooth] for $f$ on the first and on the second thickening, carrying solutions to solutions (both triangles are preserved by composing with the isomorphisms). So $f$ has the lifting property of [def-sbc-formally-smooth] for one of them iff it has it for the other.

proof.text: *($\Rightarrow$).* Assume $f$ is formally smooth [def-sbc-formally-smooth]. Let $D$ be a ring with $\beta:R\to D$, $N\subseteq D$ with $N^2=0$, $q:D\to D/N$, and $g:S\to D/N$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras, $g\circ\varphi=q\circ\beta$. By the second step, $i=\operatorname{Spec}q:T=\operatorname{Spec}(D/N)\to T'=\operatorname{Spec}D$ is a first order thickening of affine schemes over $Y$ (via $\operatorname{Spec}\beta$). The morphism $a=\operatorname{Spec}g:T\to X$ is over $Y$: $f\circ a=\operatorname{Spec}(g\circ\varphi)=\operatorname{Spec}(q\circ\beta)=\operatorname{Spec}\beta\circ i$ (first step). Formal smoothness gives $a':T'\to X$ over $Y$ with $a'\circ i=a$. By the first step $a'=\operatorname{Spec}h$ for a unique ring map $h:S\to D$; $a'$ being over $Y$ means $h$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras, and $\operatorname{Spec}(q\circ h)=\operatorname{Spec}h\circ\operatorname{Spec}q=a'\circ i=a=\operatorname{Spec}g$ gives $q\circ h=g$ by uniqueness. So $\varphi$ satisfies the lifting condition of Algebra, Definition 00TI.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 02H4 (lemma-affine-formally-smooth, line 3164), proof: 'immediate from the definitions (Definition 02H0 and Algebra, Definition 00TI) by the equivalence of categories of rings and affine schemes, Schemes, Lemma 01I2'

proof.text: *($\Leftarrow$).* Assume $\varphi$ satisfies the lifting condition of Algebra 00TI. Let $T\subset T'$ be a first order thickening of affine schemes over $Y$ with structure morphism $b:T'\to Y$ and $a:T\to X$ with $f\circ a=b\circ i$. By the third and fourth steps we may assume $T'=\operatorname{Spec}D$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}(D/N)$ with $N^2=0$, $i=\operatorname{Spec}q$ and $b=\operatorname{Spec}\beta$ for $\beta:R\to D$. By the first step $a=\operatorname{Spec}g$ for a unique ring map $g:S\to D/N$, and $\operatorname{Spec}(g\circ\varphi)=f\circ a=b\circ i=\operatorname{Spec}(q\circ\beta)$ gives $g\circ\varphi=q\circ\beta$: $g$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $S\to D/N$. The lifting condition gives an $R$-algebra map $h:S\to D$ with $q\circ h=g$. Put $a'=\operatorname{Spec}h:T'\to X$. Then $f\circ a'=\operatorname{Spec}(h\circ\varphi)=\operatorname{Spec}\beta=b$, so $a'$ is over $Y$, and $a'\circ i=\operatorname{Spec}(q\circ h)=\operatorname{Spec}g=a$. Hence every such lifting problem has a solution and $f$ is formally smooth [def-sbc-formally-smooth].
